R6J-bear-drive-0002.name: 2.1 km SE of Gilmore Lake
R6J-bear-drive-0002.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R6J-bear-drive-0002.parkWhat: pull off on Gilmore Lake FSR (gravel road)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2020 (6 years old), 60 m N: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2018 (fire R22298), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SW facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 40 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

R6J-grouse-walk-0002.recDirections: Driving directions to the staging area: From downtown Houston head east on Highway 16 and turn off onto Butler Avenue. Follow this road to the end, then turn left onto Riverbank Drive. Follow it to the end and turn right at the four-way stop onto Omineca Way. About one kilometre later, turn left up Equity Mine Road. Go 20 kilometres and watch for the parking lot on the left-hand side.
